title: cross_artifact_inconsistency remedy re-bounces at 56% — the advance-block wrapper lists drifts but gives no source-of-truth route or anti-retry framing, so agents re-run gate advance unchanged
detail: prusik bounces (fleet ledger, 189 events) ranks cross_artifact_inconsistency at 19/34 = 56% wasted re-bounces — tied for the worst remedy-quality rate and, unlike unmet_exit_artifacts (fb-c76ae6da2255) and writable_scope (v0.205.0 rewrite), NOTHING targets it. Root cause: the advance-block wrapper (gate.py, the 'cross-artifact inconsistencies:' branch) prints the per-item strings but adds no framing that each item is a DECLARED-vs-CONTAINED drift requiring a source-of-truth edit, and — critically — no statement that re-running 'gate advance' without changing an artifact/worktree re-fires the block BYTE-IDENTICALLY. Agents re-bounce because the message doesn't say 'change X on disk, then advance'. The worktrees_clean_of_cache_artifacts item also buries its immediate fix (delete the cache dir now) under next-time prevention advice. Fix: rewrite the wrapper remedy in the v0.205.0 writable_scope mold — name the reconciliation route per drift-type + explicit don't-retry — keeping the gate_class + detection unchanged so 'prusik bounces' re-measurement is a clean before/after.

resolution.verify: CUR=$(prusik --version 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+[.][0-9]+[.][0-9]+' | head -1); [ -n "$CUR" ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' '0.211.0' "$CUR" | sort -V | head -1)" = '0.211.0' ] && echo "1 passed: engine carries moat-proven fix fb-25937f6926fa (prusik $CUR >= 0.211.0)"
